newsitem.title: USA: SIS to buy Glastonbury bank for $41 million.
newsitem.headline: SIS to buy Glastonbury bank for $41 million.

text.p: SIS Bancorp Inc. said Monday it agreed to buy all of the outstanding shares of Glastonbury Bank & Trust Co. in a deal valued at almost $41.0 million.
Under the agreement, SIS will offer 0.75 share of its common stock for each of the Glastonbury, Conn.-based commercial bank's 1.83 million common shares in a tax-free pooling of interests.
SIS stock edged down 12.5 cents at $29.875 on the New York Stock Exchange and Glastonbury rose $1.25 to $21.25 on Nasdaq.

SIS expects to take a pretax charge of $2.5 million in 1997 to cover merger related expenses. It also expects the merger to boost earnings per share in 1998 and beyond, the company said in a statement.
In connection with the merger, SIS directors have rescinded their existing authorization for SIS to repurchase up to 286,180 shares of SIS common stock, it added.
Glastonbury, with $261.3 million in assets, would become a wholly owned subsidiary of SIS, the company said.
SIS, based in Springfield, Mass., said the deal is subject to approval by both companies' shareholders.
